traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960), as Franseria dumosa: a shrub 2 dm to 6 dm (0.2 m to 0.6 m) high.

generator.params.spur_leaf.note: A short shoot's leaf card, a little smaller than a long shoot's (leaf_size), within Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960): leaves 1 to 3 cm long.

generator.params.leaf_size.note: Leaf card length, petiole included, sized so every leaf drawn stays within Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960, as Franseria dumosa): leaves 1 to 3 cm long (0.05 drew them 4 to 4.5 cm).

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Ambrosia dumosa (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.78 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 2 records in 2 sources); trunks 0.85, branches 0.68. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long. Fitted so the tallest of five plants (seeds 1 to 5) stays within Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960, as Franseria dumosa): 20 to 60 cm tall. Fitted to the oldest reference size at 0.285, plants reached 65 cm.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a low, rounded, grey-white shrub 30 to 60 cm tall, densely branched, with small, finely lobed leaves dropped in drought; the commonest shrub of the creosote flats. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 45 cm at 6 years and 60 cm at 20. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: pale grey-white stems and leaves.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Franseria dumosa (p. 151): a shrub 2-6 dm high.

traits.woodiness.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Franseria dumosa (p. 151): a rigidly branched shrub with white bark.

traits.life_span.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Franseria dumosa (p. 151): a shrub.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Franseria dumosa (p. 151): leaves 1-3 cm long counting the usually short, slender petiole.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Franseria dumosa (p. 151): leaf outline oblong to ovate or deltoid.

traits.leaf_division.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Franseria dumosa (p. 151): one blade cut two or three times pinnately into few small obtuse divisions.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Franseria dumosa (p. 151): bi- to tripinnately divided into small ovate or obovate divisions.

traits.division_pattern.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Franseria dumosa (p. 151): pinnately divided.

traits.division_order.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Franseria dumosa (p. 151): bi- to tripinnately divided.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Franseria dumosa (p. 151): terminal racemes or raceme-like panicles, usually 5 cm long or less, staminate and pistillate heads often mixed.

traits.involucre_diameter_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Franseria dumosa (p. 151): staminate heads 3-5 mm thick, the involucre bluntly 6-9-lobed to about the middle.

traits.disc_florets.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Franseria dumosa (p. 151): staminate heads about 20-30-flowered (pistillate heads 2-flowered).

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Franseria dumosa (p. 151): the fruiting bur ovoid or spindle-shaped, 4-6 mm long, 2-beaked, with about 25-40 flat straight spines 2.5-4 mm long.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4, Franseria dumosa (p. 151): April to November.

traits.fruiting_months.note: Seed Manual, Ambrosia chapter (printed p. 243): blooming "primarily from February to June" and seeds "mature 3 to 4 months after flowering"; read as May to October. FEIS's white bursage review (Marshall 1994) gives no seed-ripening dates.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.note: The blade drawn dissected (spec rework E1), as Abrams and Ferris describe it, twice or thrice pinnately cut into small rounded lobes: a twice-divided card whose segments run together along a winged rachis, the running together from its incision by the rules at the flowering plants. About 3 pairs of primary segments, each cut into 5 lobes, by eye from photographs; before, a three-lobed blade.

traits.leaf_habit.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L3119493), as no source read gives it.

traits.rosette.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L3119493), as no source read gives it.

traits.leaf_margin.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L3119493), as no source read gives it.

generator.params.bloom_area.note: The leaf area its `bloom` look draws on an organ 1 m long (plantc's shading-area test), so it shades with what it shows, now that the look follows the species' stated facts (was 0.478).
